panels.title: TR 101 290 in sync
panels.description: compliance_probe_tr101290_in_sync — 1 while the ConformanceMonitor's TS_sync_loss hysteresis (indicator 1.1) considers the fed packet stream in sync.

panels.title: TS packets analysed / s
panels.description: rate(compliance_probe_ts_packets_total[$__rate_interval]) — volume actually fed to the conformance monitor and PCR tracker.

panels.title: ByteTap Lagged / s
panels.description: rate(compliance_probe_tap_lagged_total[$__rate_interval]) — non-zero means the wire-level TR 101 290 continuity-count/PCR analysis is gapped across the lost stretch (see media_plane::ByteTap docs). Never expected to be non-zero on a healthy probe.

panels.description: rate(compliance_probe_event_cursor_lagged_total[$__rate_interval]) — non-zero means SCTE-35 cues were evicted from the Trunk event log before this probe polled them.

panels.title: What this dashboard does NOT show

options.content:
**Not monitored, on purpose — a green panel here would be a lie:**
- TR 101 290 `PCR_accuracy_error` (2.4): never emitted by `dvb-conformance` (needs ±500ns hardware timing). The "PCR rate estimate" row below is **not** this.
- T-STD `Buffer_error`/`Empty_buffer_error`/`Data_delay_error`: partial (see `dvb-conformance` README) **and clock-sensitive** — see below.
- SCTE-35 malformed-section detection on the Trunk-cursor path: structurally unobservable (event already parsed upstream).

**The arrival clock is an input to the result.** Most TR 101 290 indicators are timeout-based, so a host feeding a synthetic or stalled clock changes what fires. Measured instance: on `m6-single.ts`, a degenerate clock yields 911 events and a realistic one 876 — the whole 35-event gap being T-STD `Buffer_error`. `Continuity_count_error` is clock-independent. See `tests/wasm_analyzer_equivalence.rs`.

**Multiple feeds/routes:** this crate's metrics carry no `route` label of their own — a `Probe` doesn't know which stream it is watching. Running one probe (and one `metrics` recorder/process) per feed and distinguishing them via a Prometheus `external_labels`/scrape-job label, or via a host like `multimux` that already labels its own metrics by `route`, is the host's job, not this crate's.

panels.title: Priority 1 events/s (necessary for decodability)
panels.description: TS_sync_loss, Sync_byte_error, PAT_error_2, Continuity_count_error, PMT_error_2, PID_error.

alert.name: TR 101 290 priority-1 indicator firing
alert.message: A priority-1 (necessary-for-decodability) TR 101 290 indicator is firing.

panels.title: Priority 2 events/s (continuous/periodic monitoring)
panels.description: Transport_error, CRC_error, PCR_repetition_error, PCR_discontinuity_indicator_error, PTS_error, CAT_error. PCR_accuracy_error never appears — see the text panel above.

panels.title: Priority 3 events/s (application-dependent monitoring)
panels.description: NIT/SDT/EIT/RST/TDT_error, SI_repetition_error, Unreferenced_PID, Buffer_error, Empty_buffer_error, Data_delay_error. TWO CAVEATS: (a) the T-STD sub-checks are partial — see the dvb-conformance README; (b) Buffer_error/Empty_buffer_error/Data_delay_error are statements about ARRIVAL TIMING, so they are only as trustworthy as the arrival clock the host feeds the probe. A host feeding a synthetic or stalled clock can make these fire (or vanish) with no change in the stream. Continuity_count_error, by contrast, is clock-independent.

panels.title: PCR rate estimate — NOT ETSI TR 101 290 (this is not indicator 2.4)
Read this before interpreting the two panels to the right

options.content:
### These are NOT TR 101 290 indicator 2.4

TR 101 290 §5.2 Table 5.0b **2.4 `PCR_accuracy_error`** asks whether a PCR's *value* is within **±500 ns** of the true 27 MHz System Clock (ISO/IEC 13818-1 §2.4.2.2). That needs a hardware reference clock. **It is not measured anywhere on this dashboard, and `dvb-conformance` never emits it.**

The two panels here answer a *different, weaker* question: does this PID's PCR **advance at the same rate** as packets actually arrive, judged against the caller's own software arrival clock? That catches encoder/mux clock-rate drift and delivery-rate variation — it does **not** certify PCR accuracy, and must never be cited as 2.4 conformance.

**A flat 0 ppm here does not mean 2.4 passes.** 2.4 was not checked.

panels.title: [non-spec] PCR rate drift (smoothed, ppm) by PID
panels.description: compliance_probe_pcr_drift_ppm — this crate's own software-clock estimate of signalled-PCR-interval vs. wall-clock arrival rate. NOT TR 101 290 indicator 2.4 (PCR_accuracy_error), which requires ±500 ns hardware timing and is not measured at all. See the text panel to the left.

panels.title: [non-spec] PCR rate jitter (ppm) by PID
panels.description: compliance_probe_pcr_jitter_ppm — instantaneous deviation of the latest PCR interval error from the smoothed drift to the left. NOT TR 101 290 indicator 2.4. See the text panel.

panels.title: Cues arriving/s by kind
panels.description: compliance_probe_scte35_cues_total{kind=...} — break_start/break_end (wire and Trunk-cursor paths) or other/immediate.

panels.title: Malformed sections/s (wire path only)
panels.description: compliance_probe_scte35_malformed_total — only observable via Probe::feed_scte35_section; structurally always 0 on the Trunk-cursor path.

panels.title: Cues arriving already in the past /s
panels.description: compliance_probe_scte35_pts_in_past_total — a cue whose target pts_time had already elapsed when checked. Should be 0 on a healthy feed.

panels.title: Unresolved-anchor / no-reference-now /s (Trunk-cursor path)
panels.description: compliance_probe_scte35_unresolved_anchor_total (the cue's own EventAnchor is still Segment/Utc) and compliance_probe_scte35_no_reference_total (Probe::note_media_time was never called) — never fabricated, always counted instead.

panels.title: Structural findings/s by rule + severity
panels.description: compliance_probe_structural_findings_total{rule_id=...,severity=...} — from crate::structural::run_structural_checks. Whole-buffer-shaped, not per-packet: see that module's docs for cadence caveats.
